given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)

breaks.break: Loans due before today are skipped (overdue test inverted or too strict)
A loan due today is treated as overdue (`<=`)
A returned loan is treated as open
'Today' is taken from the wrong day or timezone

given.why: The test uses one day-granular case with a one-day overdue margin and never checks a UTC date boundary, so a timezone slip would pass.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today

breaks.break: A loan with no reminder at all is skipped
A reminder recorded on an earlier day is treated as today's, so the loan is never reminded again

given.why: No test seeds a reminder from a previous day, so a code that blocks on any past reminder would pass every test.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member

breaks.break: Never calls the API
Sends loanId in place of memberId
Sends the wrong dueOn
Sends a reminder for only some of the overdue loans

then.why: The test checks each sent record's member, loan and due date, and the count of records.

then.part: then records a reminder for today

breaks.break: Records nothing
Records dueOn instead of today
Records for the wrong loan

then.why: The test reads the reminders table and checks the loan ids, the sent_on of 2026-03-17 and the count.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today

breaks.break: The dedupe check is dropped or inverted, so the second run resends
The check uses `sent_on < today`, so today's reminder isn't matched
A reminder from an earlier day is treated as today's and suppresses the send

given.why: A same-day rerun is covered, but the nearby case of a reminder recorded yesterday is never set up.

breaks.break: The returned filter is dropped

given.why: A loan that is overdue and returned is made, and the exact-length assertion would fail if it were sent.

breaks.break: A loan due today is treated as overdue (`<=`)
The overdue filter is dropped

given.why: The loan lent on 03-03 is due exactly today, which is the boundary case.

breaks.break: Sends for the already-reminded loan
Sends for the returned loan
Sends for the not-yet-overdue loan

then.why: The sent list must match exactly one entry, loan1, after two runs, so any extra send fails.

breaks.break: A refusal is treated as accepted

given.why: The fake refuses loan1, and the table and log assertions would fail if the refusal were treated as success.

breaks.break: An unreachable API throws and aborts the job instead of becoming a refusal

given.why: B5 proves a failed connection is turned into a refused delivery, which B3's service path then handles identically.

breaks.break: Records the reminder even when refused

then.why: The reminders table must contain only loan2's row.

then.part: logs `reminder.failed` at `warn` with `loanId` and the refusal's `error`

breaks.break: Wrong event name
Wrong level
Wrong loanId, such as the member id
Hardcoded or missing error text
No log written

then.why: toContainEqual matches the whole entry exactly, and the reason is set specially in the fake.

then.part: carries on with the other loans

breaks.break: The job stops or throws at the first refusal

then.why: loan1 is refused first because it has the earlier due date, and loan2 must still be sent.

The summary is not logged when the job has nothing to do

given.why: Only a run with three overdue loans is tested; a run with no overdue loans is not.

Wrong level
Sent count not incremented, or failures counted as sent
Failed count not incremented
The finish entry is not the last log

then.why: The last log entry must equal the exact event, level and fields, with sent 2 and failed 1 distinguishing the two counts.

The base URL is ignored

then.part: any other answer or a failed connection as refused

breaks.break: Only 5xx is refused
A failed connection throws or counts as accepted

then.why: A 400 answer and a network error each produce an exact refused result.

The unreachable reason doesn't say unreachable
